rows.label: Round 1
rows.text: Add a big terracotta pot with a small lemon tree full of yellow lemons next to the blue door. Keep everything else exactly the same.

rows.label: Round 2
rows.text: Add warm string lights hanging along the edge of the roof. Keep everything else exactly the same.

rows.label: Round 3
rows.text: Add a ginger cat sleeping on the wicker armchair. Keep everything else exactly the same.

rows.label: Round 4
rows.text: Make it evening at sunset: a warm orange and pink sky, and the string lights glowing. Keep everything else exactly the same.

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Each round edits the RESULT of the round before, so the changes add up: a lemon tree, then string lights, then a cat on the chair, then sunset with the lights on. This is what loops are for: something a list cannot do, because a list always starts from the same picture.

 Steps

  1. Load your start picture.
  2. Write one change per row in Prompt Multi Pixaroma (keep it on List mode).
  3. Set total on Loop Start Pixaroma to the number of rows.
  4. Press Run once.

 How a loop works

  • Everything between Loop Start and Loop End runs again and again: total on Loop Start says how many rounds.
  • Loop Start's index says which round it is, counting from 0 (0, 1, 2, 3). A Math Expression turns it into what you need: a + 1 for 1, 2, 3, 4, or a + b to add it to a seed.
  • The value slots carry things from one round to the next. What you plug into Loop End's value1 comes out of Loop Start's value1 in the NEXT round. After the last round it comes out of Loop End.
  • Wire Loop Start's loop output into Loop End's loop input: that is how the two know they belong together.

 Writing the changes

  • ONE change per round works best: Add ..., Make it ..., Remove ....
  • End each one with Keep everything else exactly the same. so the earlier changes stay.
  • Small things add up: after many rounds the picture slowly drifts. 4 to 6 rounds is a good amount.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Nodes look different from the video

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Flux 2 Klein 9B) - The image model, Flux 2 Klein 9B from Black Forest Labs. It is a fast 4-step model that can make a picture from words AND change a picture you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen 3 8B, reads the prompt) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the image model understands.
  • Load VAE (Flux 2) - Turns the finished render into a picture you can see, and a picture into the model's own format.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (1. start picture) - The picture you start from. Round 1 edits this picture.
  • Longest Side Pixaroma (2. work size) - Makes the longest side 1024, near the 1 megapixel Klein works best at. Its width and height also go to the blank canvas.
  • Prompt Multi Pixaroma (3. one change per round, List mode) - One CHANGE per row, in List mode. Row 1 is done in round 1, row 2 in round 2, and so on.
  • Seed Pixaroma (4. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.
  • Loop Start Pixaroma (5. how many rounds) - Opens the loop. total = how many rounds (4). value1 carries the picture: round 1 gets your picture, every later round gets the RESULT of the round before. value2 carries the pile of all results.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves and do the small jobs: count, pick, join or pass things along.

  • Math Expression (round number = index + 1) - Turns the round number into a row number: a + 1, because the index counts from 0 and the list from 1.
  • Prompt From List Pixaroma (this round's change) - Picks this round's change from the list by its number.
  • Combine Pixaroma (adds this round to the pile) - Adds this round's result to the pile, so you can see every step at the end.
  • Loop End Pixaroma (sends the result to the next round) - Closes the loop. The new picture goes into value1, so the next round edits it; the pile goes into value2.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • CLIP Text Encode (reads the edit prompt) - Reads the prompt through the text encoder.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. Klein runs at CFG 1, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • VAE Encode (picture to latent) - Turns your picture into the model's format so Klein can look at it.
  • ReferenceLatent (your picture, positive) - Hands your picture to Klein as the picture to edit. There are two, one for the prompt and one for the empty negative, and both get the same picture.
  • ReferenceLatent (your picture, negative) - Hands your picture to Klein as the picture to edit. There are two, one for the prompt and one for the empty negative, and both get the same picture.
  • Empty Flux 2 Latent (blank canvas) - The blank canvas the picture is painted on, at the size it receives.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings Klein is made for.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Preview Image Pixaroma (every round, saved) - Shows every round, step by step, and saves them into ComfyUI/output/Loop Build Up.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the number of pictures and their size.

RoundsSizeTime
4 (the demo)1024 x 1024about 13 s
Each round you add1024 x 1024about 3 s more

Klein needs 4 steps, so it is fast: about 1.7 s for a 1024 x 1024 picture from a prompt and about 3 s for an edit at 1 megapixel, where it also reads your picture.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models from disk (about 18 GB for Klein and its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a 16 GB card

Timed on an RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB with 32 GB of RAM:

  • Klein took about 3 to 6 times as long, about 10 s even for one picture: Klein and its text encoder (17 GB together) do not fit in 16 GB, so parts of them load again on every Run, and a second Run is no faster.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
